expectations.name: s6b_stays_at_warn_not_trip
expectations.detail: dut:K4_open never observed before the boundary [blocked_on annotation is STALE: this expectation now passes -- the DUT appears to have gained the capability the annotation assumed it lacked; consider removing blocked_on from the scenario]

blocked_on.reason: This forbid clause is currently satisfied for the wrong reason: K4 starts de-energized (open) at boot and stays that way -- relay_owner_command_energize() is fully built (firmware/SaftyFW/src/tasks/relay_owner.c) but called by nothing in the current source tree -- so K4_open is already true at sim-time 0. Separately, link_up is never set true because safety_core_build_input() never populates it (the struct literal has no .link_up entry at all -- confirmed by reading safety_core.c), so S6b's own unconditional ~120s hard-backstop trip (link_dead_hard_s default) would also eventually fire in any run long enough to reach sim_end regardless of this blip's own current/link behavior -- two independent reasons this cannot currently validate the 'stays at warn, not trip' claim it names.
blocked_on.phase: For K4 energize: link_task exists but has no LINK_FRAME_REQUEST_ENABLE_CMD case (SAFETY_CMD_REQUEST_ENABLE 0x02, already sent by KilnFW) -- a genuinely missing decoder, Phase 7 work not yet done. For link_up: unlike context_valid (which link_task already produces via link_task_get_context_snapshot(), just unread by safety_core_build_input()), link_up has no producer/getter in link_task.{c,h} at all yet -- link_task.h's own doc comment on link_task_get_degraded_no_context() confirms Phase 7's context-dependent-guard wiring is still future work. Both are Phase 7 gaps, but not the same gap as each other, and neither is 'link_task does not exist' -- link_task is built and handles PUSH_CONTEXT/CLEAR_TRIP/SET_CONFIG/ROLLBACK/ ANNOUNCE_REBOOT/ANNOUNCE_VERSION/FW_VERSION already.
